pages: This is a made-up document for building and testing only. The Burning and Suppression of Solids experiment burned thin fabric samples inside a small chamber on a space station.
In microgravity, flames on thin fabrics spread more slowly upstream than in normal gravity because there is no buoyant flow. A gentle airflow from a fan supplied fresh oxygen to the flame.
When the airflow was turned down, some flames shrank and went out. The samples that kept burning had flames that looked dim and rounded instead of tall and bright.
This is a made-up document for building and testing only. The Flame Extinguishment experiment ignited small fuel droplets that floated freely without any support.
Heptane droplets showed cool-flame burning after the visible flame went out, a behavior rarely seen on Earth. The cool flame gave off almost no light but kept slowly consuming the fuel.
This is a made-up document for building and testing only. The Spacecraft Fire Experiment tested fires much larger than any that can be lit safely on a crewed station.
Large cotton-fiberglass samples burned in an uncrewed cargo vehicle; flame spread rate rose with airflow speed. Sensors recorded how the fire changed oxygen and temperature in the cabin air.
